newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Norfolk Southern promise to preserve jobs.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Norfolk Southern promise to preserve jobs.

text.p: The CEOs of CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp told a Senate committee Thursday they intended to preserve most jobs and expand facilities in New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Maryland if a deal goes through resulting in the acquisition and breakup of Conrail Inc.
"We're making a major bet on growth," David Goode, CEO of Norfolk Southern, told a Senate Appropriations subcommittee.
Goode said the acquisition would work for his railroad because he believed it would promote growth and "that's going to be jobs."

Both Goode and SCX CEO John Snow pledged to retain a variety of facilities in cities and towns in the three states. They also pledged to improve facilities into the ports of Newark, N.J., and Philadelphia.
They also promised to expand competitive facilities into the port of Baltimore.
In addition, both said they would have other significant facilities in Philadelphia.
The CEOs had been pressed by senators from the three states who said they were concerned about preserving jobs.
